messages:
Kevin H: Escalation from acct team: customer onboarding CI started failing after migration to shared VPC/transit gateway. Agent logs show model shard pulls returning 403 and pip pulls timing out. They say nothing changed for the app itself.

Acct Team: Sending initial details — NAT IPs: 52.12.34.56, 52.12.34.57. They attached a short snippet from the failing CI job.

Customer-Network-Eng: Paste of agent log:
```
2026-04-01T08:14:22Z agent: GET https://model-registry.redwood.ai/v1/shards/abcd -> 403 Forbidden
2026-04-01T08:14:23Z pip: GET https://files.pythonhosted.org/... -> Operation timed out
```

Maria S: Can the customer run a direct curl from the failing runner and include -v output? Also ask them to run openssl s_client with SNI to see the presented cert.

Kevin H: Customer returned this curl -v from the CI host:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" https://model-registry.redwood.ai/v1/shards/abcd
* Connected to model-registry.redwood.ai (10.1.0.45) port 443 (#0)
* TLSv1.2 (IN), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
*  server certificate verify OK
< HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
```
Also ran openssl s_client:
```
openssl s_client -connect model-registry.redwood.ai:443 -servername model-registry.redwood.ai -showcerts
# certificate subject: CN=corp-intercept.local
# subjectAltName: DNS:corp-intercept.local
```

Lee C: That cert shows TLS interception by their security stack and their split-horizon DNS is resolving our host to an internal IP (10.1.0.45). Two likely failure modes: the proxy rewrites certs (breaking token validation/OIDC calls) or their proxy is stripping/rewriting Authorization headers leading to 403 from our registry.

Maria S: Short triage checklist for them to run and report back:
1) From a failing host: curl -v --resolve model-registry.redwood.ai:443:54.240.10.12 https://model-registry.redwood.ai/v1/health
   - If this returns our cert CN and a 200, then DNS resolution was the issue.
2) openssl s_client -connect auth.redwood.ai:443 -servername auth.redwood.ai -showcerts
   - Confirm auth.redwood.ai cert is our certificate (no corporate intercept).
3) tcpdump of the failed TLS handshake (pcap) if they can share.

Kevin H: Customer confirmed the corp-intercept cert persists even when forcing public IP via /etc/hosts. So proxy is doing TLS MITM downstream of DNS too.

Lee C: For immediate unblocking we can recommend two approaches (short-term vs recommended):
- Short-term: Add host-level /etc/hosts entries to force public IPs for redwood endpoints in CI and disable proxy for those requests (only temporary and not ideal for security/compliance).
- Recommended: Configure their Zscaler / proxy policy to bypass TLS inspection for our service FQDNs and allow CONNECT/TCP passthrough on 443 for these hosts.

Maria S: Minimal FQDN allowlist we ask customers to bypass TLS-inspect/proxy for (TCP 443 unless noted):
- model-registry.redwood.ai
- models.redwood.ai
- auth.redwood.ai
- api.redwood.ai
- telemetry.redwood.ai
- download.redwood.ai
- files.pythonhosted.org
- pypi.org
- sts.amazonaws.com
- s3.amazonaws.com and regional S3 endpoints used in shard URIs

Kevin H: Also provided the NAT egress IPs so their network team can whitelist those on their side if needed. We can also whitelist their NATs on our side for debugging if they want. NATs again: 52.12.34.56, 52.12.34.57.

Lee C: Note for their infra: IP-based bypass is sometimes not enough because some proxies still intercept by IP. Hostname-based bypass (SNI or explicit proxy rules) is the most reliable way to avoid MITM for these flows.

Maria S: Drafted a minimal JSON snippet they can paste into a firewall change request:
```
{
  "bypass_hosts": [
    "model-registry.redwood.ai",
    "auth.redwood.ai",
    "models.redwood.ai",
    "api.redwood.ai",
    "telemetry.redwood.ai"
  ],
  "ports": [443]
}
```

Kevin H: Customer asks about the pypi timeouts — recommend a small set of CDNs to allow:
- files.pythonhosted.org
- pypi.org
- hooks.python.org

oncall-bot: Ticket #5789 created and assigned to infra-priv-deploys. Acknowledged at 2026-04-01T08:18:05Z.

Acct Team: Scheduling network call with customer (Zscaler + infra) tomorrow. They will collect a pcap and provide vendor/firmware details.

Lee C: If they implement the bypass and still see 403s, collect full agent debug logs (enable DEBUG on agent) and the exact curl with -v and -D - so we can inspect headers. If Authorization headers are being stripped or modified, that will explain 401/403 behavior.

Maria S: I'll assemble a KB link with vendor-specific guidance for Zscaler/F5/PaloAlto and the recommended firewall rules. Also will DM the team our current ELB and S3 CIDR ranges so they can use IPs if they prefer.

Kevin H: Noting Jira 112233 for reference. Leaving notes in the ticket. :thumbsup:
